identity.name: Magnesium salts of fatty acids
identity.chemical_class: Magnesium salts of long-chain fatty acids (fatty-acid carboxylates; soap-like emulsifier/anticaking agents)

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic magnesium fatty-acid salts reduce particle-particle friction and interfacial tension, improving powder flow/anticaking and emulsification behavior.

adi.basis: EFSA (2018) concluded there is no need for a numerical ADI for E470a/E470b and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.

efsa.key_finding: E470b is authorised in the EU; EFSA found no safety concern at reported uses/use levels, including dedicated infant (>12 weeks) considerations in the re-evaluation.

fda.notes: 21 CFR 184.1440 affirms magnesium stearate as GRAS with GMP-limited use; 21 CFR 172.863 permits magnesium salts of fatty acids as binder/emulsifier/anticaking agent under GMP.

adi.basis: JECFA magnesium stearate record lists ADI NOT SPECIFIED (latest evaluation year 2020; 2015 entry reaffirmed ADI not specified for magnesium salts of stearic/palmitic acids).

concerns.summary: EFSA noted limited dedicated subchronic/chronic/reproductive/developmental toxicity datasets for salts of fatty acids and relied on available supporting toxicology/read-across.
A single case report described urticarial allergic reaction attributed to magnesium stearate, indicating possible rare hypersensitivity.
A 2017 test battery (Ames, chromosome aberration, micronucleus) reported no genotoxic signal for magnesium stearate at tested conditions.

A pharmacoepidemiologic study reported worse outcomes for magnesium-stearate-containing aspirin formulations, suggesting formulation interaction concerns outside direct food-additive toxicity context.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2018: no need for numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels for E470a/E470b.
JECFA: ADI NOT SPECIFIED for magnesium stearate / magnesium salts context.
US CFR: magnesium stearate affirmed GRAS (21 CFR 184.1440) with GMP conditions.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI is set by EFSA or JECFA for this additive; EFSA re-evaluation did not identify a safety concern at reported use levels.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus supports low concern at permitted food-use levels (EFSA no numerical ADI needed, JECFA ADI not specified, US CFR GRAS/GMP framework), but data gaps and rare hypersensitivity signals argue against categorizing as fully risk_free.
key_factors: EFSA 2018 no-safety-concern conclusion with no numerical ADI
JECFA ADI not specified and latest 2020 evaluation entry
US CFR GRAS status and GMP-limited conditions (21 CFR 184.1440; 172.863)
No IARC classification entry found for magnesium stearate/E470b
Sparse dedicated long-term human safety data and isolated allergy report
